documents.text: Incident report A states the collision occurred on 2026-02-01 at approximately 3:15pm at the intersection of 5th and Main, front-end impact. Incident report B, filed by the same claimant two days later, describes the collision as occurring on 2026-02-02 at approximately 8:45am on Route 9, a rear-end impact instead. Adjuster notes reference a third possible date of 2026-01-30 based on a witness statement that may or may not pertain to this claim. Vehicle make and model are consistent across all three documents but the damage location described differs each time: front-end in report A, rear bumper in report B, and 'driver side, extent unclear' in the adjuster notes. No single document is internally contradictory, but the three taken together describe what could be as many as three separate incidents or one incident described inconsistently three times.

Estimate 1 (from report A's shop): front bumper, headlight, hood — $15,000. Estimate 2 (from report B's shop, submitted separately): rear bumper, trunk, tail lights — $11,200. The two estimates do not describe the same damage and neither references the other.

ground_truth.notes: Deliberately ambiguous/contradictory documents designed to stress the loop guard and step/budget ceilings rather than resolve cleanly.
